claims.text: ConcurrencyLimiter allows at most PermitLimit leases at once; a lease is held until disposed. Up to QueueLimit further requests wait for a permit; a request that finds the queue full is rejected at once.
claims.source_hint: API reference: System.Threading.RateLimiting.ConcurrencyLimiter, ConcurrencyLimiterOptions (PermitLimit, QueueLimit); ASP.NET Core docs: Rate limiting middleware, 'Concurrency limiter'

claims.text: The rate limiting middleware acquires the lease before the endpoint runs and releases it when the request ends, so a concurrency limiter counts requests in progress, not requests per period.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Rate limiting middleware, 'Concurrency limiter' (limits concurrent requests)

claims.text: options.AddConcurrencyLimiter(policyName, configure) registers a policy backed by one ConcurrencyLimiter shared by every request to endpoints using that policy (no per-caller partition).
claims.source_hint: API reference: Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting.RateLimiterOptionsExtensions.AddConcurrencyLimiter; Rate limiting middleware docs

claims.text: RateLimiterOptions.RejectionStatusCode defaults to 503; a ConcurrencyLimiter's failed lease carries no MetadataName.RetryAfter, so Program.cs's OnRejected (lines 173-181) leaves the status at 503.
claims.source_hint: API reference: RateLimiterOptions.RejectionStatusCode; ConcurrencyLimiter (failed lease metadata); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 DonHang.Api/Program.cs lines 168-181

Npgsql pools connections by default; Maximum Pool Size defaults to 100 and the stage-3 connection string does not set it. CatalogDbContext and DonHangDbContext get the same connection string, so product reads and orders both use the api's connections to the same PostgreSQL database.

claims.text: At stage-3, with Redis stopped, a product read is answered from PostgreSQL: ProductCache treats the Redis error as a miss (abortConnect=false, BacklogPolicy.FailFast). The product list (CatalogService.ListAsync) never uses the cache; it queries CatalogDbContext every time.

At stage-3 Payments and Notifications run as separate Compose services (own containers, processes, databases donhang_payments / donhang_notifications); Notifications sends email via SMTP to mailpit; the api sends no email (Program.cs line 42).

claims.text: A request waiting in the limiter's queue is still in progress: it waits in the queue until a permit comes free (or a timeout), and its caller has no answer yet.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Rate limiting middleware, queuing ('waits in the queue until a permit becomes available or a timeout occurs')

claims.text: UseHttpMetrics (prometheus-net) records each request with its status code, so 503 refusals of product reads count among the api's 5xx answers.
claims.source_hint: prometheus-net README, ASP.NET Core HTTP request metrics; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 DonHang.Api/Program.cs lines 190-195

claims.text: bulkhead.sh @ stage-3 stops Redis, sends one POST /api/v1/orders and 100 parallel GET /api/v1/products/3, then restarts Redis; captured output: only 200/503: yes, some 503: yes, some 200: yes, order -> 201.
A Kubernetes container's resource limit caps the CPU and memory that container may use on its node.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Resource Management for Pods and Containers (limits)

claims.text: Use a concurrency cap inside one process, rather than extracting a service, when the only goal is to keep one kind of request from taking capacity another needs; a separate service adds a network call and more to deploy and watch.
Refuse at once beyond a short queue, rather than let requests wait without bound, when waiting requests hold resources and callers may give up; a short queue suits brief bursts.

At most 20 product reads run at once, so at most 20 can query PostgreSQL at once. ProductCache.FindAsync takes a per-key SemaphoreSlim, so reads of one product query one at a time; in bulkhead.sh (100 reads of product 3) the 20 permit holders wait on that lock.
claims.source_hint: Follows from claims 1, 2, 5, 6; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 DonHang.Catalog/ProductCache.cs lines 31-41

claims.text: A concurrency limiter cannot know when a running request will end, so its refused lease has no RetryAfter; Program.cs's OnRejected therefore never sets 429 for catalog-reads.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: rate-limit-samples, 'The ConcurrencyLimiter has no way of calculating when permits are available'
